attempts.summary: On node1 (RHEL 7.9), restricted cron scheduling to root and opsadmin by creating /etc/cron.allow containing only those two users. Since opsadmin did not previously exist, created it first. Verified enforcement (allowed users can use crontab, others are rejected with 'not allowed to use this program'). Performed the mandatory single-node restart: captured baseline boot_id and cron state, rebooted node1 via `shutdown -r now`, confirmed the node went unreachable then came back, verified the boot_id changed (0d6209e2... -> ece1d32b...), and confirmed crond was active and /etc/cron.allow / opsadmin's ability to schedule cron jobs (and a new test user's inability to) persisted after reboot.
